messages.author: 20a091f3d0e9ee8f
messages.subject: Covariance matrices differences
parts:
Hi dear all,

with the data Holzing HolzingerSwineford1939 I compute the covariances "manually" and using inspect(fit, "sampstat")
The differences between the two matrices are so big that I do not believe it is related to the (N-1)/N factor...
Any ideas? Thank you!!

Data9 <- HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4","x5","x6","x7","x8","x9")]
S <- cov(Data9)
round(S, 3)

Results:
> Data9 <- HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4","x5","x6","x7","x8","x9")]
> S <- cov(Data9)
> round(S, 3)
      x1     x2    x3    x4    x5    x6     x7    x8    x9
x1 1.363  0.409 0.582 0.507 0.442 0.456  0.085 0.265 0.460
x2 0.409  1.386 0.453 0.210 0.212 0.248 -0.097 0.110 0.245
x3 0.582  0.453 1.279 0.209 0.113 0.245  0.089 0.213 0.375
x4 0.507  0.210 0.209 1.355 1.101 0.899  0.220 0.126 0.244
x5 0.442  0.212 0.113 1.101 1.665 1.018  0.143 0.181 0.296
x6 0.456  0.248 0.245 0.899 1.018 1.200  0.145 0.166 0.237
x7 0.085 -0.097 0.089 0.220 0.143 0.145  1.187 0.537 0.375
x8 0.265  0.110 0.213 0.126 0.181 0.166  0.537 1.025 0.459
x9 0.460  0.245 0.375 0.244 0.296 0.237  0.375 0.459 1.018

Then I Compute the observed covariance matrix with:
inspect(fit, "sampstat"):
> inspect(fit, "sampstat")
$cov
       x1     x2     x3     y1     y2     y3     y4     y5     y6     y7     y8
x1  0.530

x3  0.812  1.782  1.950

Michael--
     In time, errors like that will become old friends. They will actually give you confidence--they become the first things you turn to when dealing with strange results, rather than panicking over some arcane computer error that is beyond your control.
     Sample size, if you are using the whole H-S dataset, is around 300, so n / n - 1 is about 1.0033. These look like differences at the third decimal place--unless I am missing something--so that seems about right.
